newsitem.title: TURKEY: Arcelik aims to attain 1996 sales level in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Arcelik aims to attain 1996 sales level in 1997.

text.p: Turkey's leading durable household goods producer Arcelik A.S. is aiming to attain its 1996 sales level of around $1.1 billion next year, a senior company official said.

"Our 1996 turnover will be realised at around $1.1 billion or 84 trillion lira and we expect it to be more than one billion dollars in 1997, close to 1996 level," general manager Mehmet Ali Berkman told Reuters in an interview.
Berkman said the real growth in Arcelik sales would be 18 percent in 1996.

"1996 was a very good year for our company, even better than 1993, which was a big step. We had good results from all our four plants," Berkman said. "So our 1996 profit will also be a very good one."
Arcelik aims to be one of the five biggest durable household goods producers in the European market in the next decade, Berkman said.
"We will have to double our production capacities to meet this target," Berkman said, "We may increase the capacity by acquiring new brands abroad or investing in the target markets."
The shares of the company, an affiliate of the industrial Koc conglomorate, opened unchanged at 11,000 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Friday.

Arcelik has a share of 67 percent in the oven market, 40 percent in the vacuum cleaner market, 58 to 59 percent in the refrigerator market, 74 percent in the dishwasher market and 63 to 64 percent in the washing machine market in Turkey.
"We aim to protect our market share in 1997 in all products," Berkman said.
Arcelik is planning to expand its product range in 1997 to protect its market share.

"For the first step, we will introduce new cheap models of washing machines to meet the soaring demand," Berkman said, "Later, we will introduce Arcelik designed dishwashers to the market to which we have been supplying Bosch designed ones so far."
He said the company's 1997 strategy would focus on introducing new and cheaper brands.

The company undertook a $90 million capacity expansion and modernisation investment in 1996. Its refrigerator production capacity climbed to 1.4 million units, washing machine capacity to 1.1 million units, oven capacity to 650,000 units and dishwasher capacity to 500,000 per year.
Arcelik's 1996 exports stood at the same level as in 1995 at $75 million.
"We will have an export attack in 1997 with new markets," Berkman said.

He said newly developing European markets -- Poland, the Czech and Slovak Republics, Ukraine, Russia, Hungary and the central Asian republics, the Middle East and north African markets -- are the alternatives for the already saturated European market.
Arcelik reported a 62 trillion lira turnover in the first nine months of 1996, compared with 34.9 trillion lira a year earlier.
The net profit of the company soared to 5.697 trillion lira in the first nine months of this year, against 1.8 trillion lira in the same period of 1995.
